summary: PlanetaryAnalogAI is an end-to-end multispectral remote sensing and machine learning pipeline that automates the "blind discovery" and quantitative characterization of Lunar and Martian geological analog sites on Earth. Trained exclusively on 12 global reference and negative control sites and tested blindly across 5 unseen sites in Türkiye, the system generates pixel-level planetary analog probability rasters, 300 DPI statistical phase-space diagnostics, and QGIS-validated geomorphological maps to accelerate analog field site selection for upcoming Artemis and Mars exploration missions.
details:
> The Challenge: Identifying terrestrial analog sites that accurately replicate the mineralogy, regolith properties, and geomorphology of the Moon and Mars traditionally relies on slow, manual literature surveys and localized expert knowledge.

> Our Solution: We developed PlanetaryAnalogAI, a five-stage modular Python pipeline (01_global_catalog.py through 04_predict.py) that transforms raw multispectral satellite imagery into actionable planetary exploration intelligence:

> * Global Reference & Negative Control Architecture: Rather than training on our target regions, we built a calibration dataset of 8 established global planetary analogs alongside 4 negative control environments (agricultural land, dense forest, urban infrastructure, and alpine terrain) to ensure the model learns true geological signatures rather than land-cover artifacts.

> * Domain-Specific Feature Engineering (02_features.py): We extracted spectral reflectance ratios, ferric iron-oxide proxies, vegetation-absence masks, and terrain texture metrics tailored to distinguish basaltic/evaporitic Martian targets from anorthositic/regolith-like Lunar targets.

> * Blind Discovery & Quantitative Validation: Evaluated blindly on 5 candidate sites in Türkiye, the model achieved clear class separation:

> * High-Priority Lunar Analogs: Levent Vadisi (Mean: 0.926, Max: 0.993) and Karanlık Kanyon (Mean: 0.907, Max: 0.993).

> * High-Priority Martian Analogs: Kula Volkanik Sahası (Max: 0.994) and Meke Krateri (Max: 0.999).

> * Dual Lunar-Martian Evaporite System: Tuz Gölü (Lunar Mean: 0.812, Martian Max: 0.954).

> * False-Positive Rejection: All 4 negative control classes were suppressed below 0.174.

> * Geospatial Verification in QGIS: Dual-band GeoTIFF probability outputs were cross-checked in QGIS against high-resolution satellite basemaps, confirming that high probability clusters precisely trace exposed canyon escarpments and volcanic cones while excluding vegetated valleys and water bodies.

> Repository & Evidence: All source scripts, requirements.txt, quantitative CSV reports, 300 DPI comparison plots, and QGIS probability maps are publicly documented at: https://github.com/hayricanonaran/PlanetaryAnalogAl
